topicName: Development of Social and Economic Formations
description: This topic examines the stages through which human societies have passed, namely communalism, slavery, feudalism and capitalism, their main features, the relations of production in each, and how one formation changed into another.

mcq.questionText: A social and economic formation refers to a particular stage in the organisation of human society based mainly on the way people:
mcq.explanation: A social-economic formation is defined by the way a society produces its material needs and the relations of production that go with it.

mcq.questionText: Which is the FIRST and earliest stage of social and economic formation in human history?
mcq.explanation: Communalism, also called primitive communal society, was the earliest stage when people lived and worked together as a group.

mcq.questionText: What is the correct order in which the social and economic formations developed?
mcq.explanation: Societies developed in the order: communalism, slavery, feudalism and then capitalism.

mcq.questionText: A main feature of the primitive communal society was that:

options.text: the means of production were owned by one rich family
the means of production were owned communally
people bought and sold one another as slaves
land was rented out by lords to tenants

mcq.explanation: In communalism the tools, land and other means of production were owned in common by the whole community.

mcq.questionText: In the primitive communal society there were NO classes mainly because:

options.text: everybody owned the means of production together
people were too few to quarrel
a king controlled all the wealth
there were strong laws against classes

mcq.explanation: Because the means of production were owned communally and there was no surplus to exploit, no classes of exploiters and exploited existed.

mcq.questionText: In the slave mode of production, the two main classes were the:
mcq.explanation: Slave society was divided into slave owners (masters), who owned everything, and slaves, who owned nothing.

mcq.questionText: In a slave society, the slave was regarded as:
mcq.explanation: The slave was treated as the property of the master, who could buy, sell or use the slave as a tool of production.

mcq.questionText: In the feudal mode of production, the main means of production was:
mcq.explanation: Under feudalism land was the most important means of production, and those who owned it controlled wealth and power.

mcq.questionText: Under feudalism, the class that owned large pieces of land was called the:
mcq.explanation: The feudal lords (landlords) owned the land, while the serfs or peasants worked on it in return for the right to use a small portion.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the relationship between a serf and a feudal lord?

options.text: The serf was the property of the lord and could be sold
The serf was paid wages in money by the lord
The serf worked on the lord's land and gave part of the produce or labour
The serf and the lord owned the land equally

mcq.explanation: A serf was tied to the land and had to give part of his produce or unpaid labour to the lord in exchange for using a piece of land.

mcq.questionText: In the capitalist mode of production, the two main classes are the:
mcq.explanation: Capitalist society is divided into capitalists who own the means of production and workers who sell their labour for wages.

mcq.questionText: Under capitalism, workers earn their living mainly by:

options.text: selling their labour power for wages

mcq.explanation: Workers under capitalism own no means of production, so they survive by selling their labour power to capitalists for wages.

mcq.questionText: The phrase 'relations of production' refers to the relationships between people in the process of:
mcq.explanation: Relations of production are the relationships that people enter into with one another while producing their material wealth.

mcq.questionText: Which formation is mainly characterised by the production of goods for sale (commodities) and the use of machines in factories?
mcq.explanation: Capitalism is marked by large-scale commodity production using machines and factories, with goods produced for sale and profit.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the BEST reason why human societies changed from one formation to another?

options.text: Changes in the religion of the people
Development of the tools and ways of producing wealth
Increase in the number of festivals

mcq.explanation: Societies changed mainly because the development of tools and methods of production created new relations of production and new classes.

fib.questionText: A particular stage in the organisation of human society based on the way people produce their needs is called a social and economic _____.
fib.explanation: Each stage of society is known as a social and economic formation.

fib.questionText: The earliest stage of human society, in which property was owned in common, is called primitive _____ society.
fib.explanation: The first formation is the primitive communal society, also called communalism.

fib.questionText: In the slave society, the person who owned the slave and the means of production was called the slave _____.
fib.explanation: The slave owner, or master, owned both the slaves and the means of production.

fib.questionText: Under feudalism, the most important means of production was _____.
fib.explanation: Land was the chief means of production in the feudal formation.

fib.questionText: A poor peasant who was tied to the land and worked for the feudal lord is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Serfs worked on the lords' land and surrendered part of their produce or labour.

fib.questionText: Under capitalism, the owners of the factories and means of production are called the _____.
fib.explanation: The capitalists, or bourgeoisie, own the means of production.

fib.questionText: Under capitalism, the workers who sell their labour for wages are together called the _____.
fib.explanation: The working class that owns no means of production is called the proletariat.

fib.questionText: The relationships people enter into while producing wealth are called the relations of _____.
fib.explanation: These are known as the relations of production.

fib.questionText: Production of goods mainly for sale on the market is known as _____ production.
fib.explanation: Goods produced for exchange or sale are called commodities, hence commodity production.

fib.questionText: In a society where there are no exploiters and no exploited people, the society is said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Communalism was a classless society because the means of production were owned in common.

tf.questionText: The primitive communal society was a classless society.
tf.explanation: There were no classes because the means of production were owned in common.

tf.questionText: In the primitive communal society, individuals owned large private farms and factories.
tf.explanation: Property was owned communally, not privately; farms and factories belong to later stages.

tf.questionText: In slave society, the slave was treated as the property of the master.
tf.explanation: Slaves were owned by masters and could be bought, sold or used as tools of production.

tf.questionText: Slavery came after capitalism in the development of social and economic formations.
tf.explanation: Slavery came before feudalism and capitalism; the order is communalism, slavery, feudalism, capitalism.

tf.questionText: Under feudalism, the feudal lords owned the land while the serfs worked on it.
tf.explanation: Feudal lords owned the land and the serfs laboured on it in return for the right to use part of it.

tf.questionText: Under feudalism, serfs were paid money wages by the lords for their labour.
tf.explanation: Serfs were not paid wages; they gave part of their produce or unpaid labour to the lords.

tf.questionText: Under capitalism, workers sell their labour power to the capitalists for wages.
tf.explanation: Workers own no means of production and survive by selling their labour for wages.

tf.questionText: The main reason societies changed from one formation to another was the development of the means and methods of production.
tf.explanation: Changes in the forces of production created new relations of production and new formations.

tf.questionText: Relations of production refer to the relationships between people during the process of producing wealth.
tf.explanation: This is the correct meaning of relations of production.

tf.questionText: Both slavery and feudalism were classless societies with no exploitation.
tf.explanation: Both slavery and feudalism had classes and exploitation; only communalism was classless.

summary.questionText: Meaning of social and economic formation
summary.correctAnswer: A stage of society based on the way people produce their needs and the relations of production.
summary.explanation: It describes how a society is organised to produce wealth.

summary.questionText: The four main social and economic formations
summary.explanation: These are the main stages societies passed through, in this order.

summary.correctAnswer: Communal ownership of the means of production with no classes.
summary.explanation: Everyone owned and worked the means of production together.
Owners controlled everything; slaves owned nothing and were treated as property.

summary.questionText: Main means of production under feudalism
summary.explanation: Whoever owned land controlled wealth and power.
Lords owned land while serfs worked on it.
Capitalists own the means of production; workers sell their labour for wages.

summary.correctAnswer: Private ownership of means of production and large-scale commodity production for profit.
summary.explanation: Goods are produced for sale using machines and factories.

summary.correctAnswer: The relationships people form with one another while producing wealth.
summary.explanation: They differ in each formation depending on who owns the means of production.

summary.questionText: Main reason societies changed from one formation to another
summary.correctAnswer: Development of the tools and methods of production.
summary.explanation: New forces of production created new relations of production and new classes.

hoq.questionText: Why is communalism described as a classless society while slavery, feudalism and capitalism are described as class societies?

options.text: Because in communalism the means of production were owned in common, with no surplus to exploit, while in the later formations a few people owned the means of production and exploited the rest
Because communalism had very few people while the others had many people
Because communalism had no leaders at all while the others had kings
Because communalism existed only in Africa while the others existed elsewhere

hoq.explanation: Common ownership in communalism prevented the rise of classes, whereas private ownership in the later formations created classes of exploiters and exploited.

hoq.questionText: How did the relationship between the producer and the owner of the means of production differ between slavery and capitalism?

options.text: In slavery the producer was owned as property and forced to work, while in capitalism the producer is legally free but must sell labour for wages
In both slavery and capitalism the producer owned the means of production
In slavery the producer was paid wages, while in capitalism the producer worked for free
In both systems the producer was given land by the owner

hoq.explanation: The slave was the property of the master, while the capitalist worker is free but owns no means of production and must sell labour for wages.

hoq.questionText: Which statement best explains why the development of better tools and methods of production led societies to move from one formation to another?

options.text: Better tools increased production and surplus, which changed who controlled wealth and created new relations of production and new classes
Better tools made people lazy so they invented new governments
Better tools reduced the population so societies had to change
Better tools were banned, forcing societies to change their stage

hoq.explanation: Improved forces of production raised output and surplus, altering ownership and relations of production and thus pushing society into a new formation.
